name: defeat
checklist_item: B. Harness -- run lifecycle: a DEFEAT resolves cleanly instead of wedging
description: The fail-safety end of the lifecycle. Drive the party to a wipe and prove the game resolves the defeat -- summary screen, no unhandled exception, no wedge.
notes: SAFETY. A run that ENDS -- win OR lose -- rewrites and can DELETE its own save (SaveGameHelper.DeleteSave). Two fixtures were destroyed that way in one session. bench.py always copies the pristine backup over GameRuns\<run_id>.ftk2 before loading, so this scenario consumes a disposable copy and the backup survives. That is not a nice-to-have here -- it is the only reason this scenario is safe to run.

crucible_kill_all is NOT used and must not be. It kills BOTH sides, which would wipe the enemies too and score a VICTORY, and it can write a DEFEAT into whatever run happens to be loaded. The defeat is produced by letting a strong enemy act.
CombatState.EndCombatEarly = true is the OPPOSITE of crucible_win_combat: it ends the fight with enemies alive and evaluates as a LOSS. Do not confuse the two.

The acceptance criterion here is fail-safety, not correctness of any number: zero unhandled exceptions, combat resolving, the session still alive afterwards. A '[ClassForge] Recipe effect failed (skipped, rest of plan continues)' line is a PASS for fail-safety and a FAIL for correctness, and bench.py reports the two separately.

fixture.notes:
REUSES THE batch-4class BED (built 2026-08-26 through real CHARACTER CREATION: Vampiric / Pacifist / Pokemon Trainer / Gary, confirmed on screen and by crucible_party_list). A dedicated bed was not built for this scenario: that party already satisfies this manifest's expect_classes and min_size, and README says extra party members do not invalidate an identity tell that names the subject. bench.py always loads a COPY, so sharing one backup across scenarios is safe as long as they run SERIALLY. Original build recipe for a dedicated bed is kept below.

ORIGINAL: BUILD RECIPE. New campaign -> CHARACTER CREATION for every slot. NEVER crucible_party_set_class: it rewrites ConfigName but not the display name, so the class is right in state and every screenshot shows a stale vanilla name -- that voided a whole verification run here. Save, copy the .ftk2 out of GameRuns\ into %USERPROFILE%\Backups\ftk2-fixtures under this name, then set status to 'built'. A DISPOSABLE one-character bed -- slot 1 = Vampiric, low level, no revival items. Never point this scenario at a fixture any other scenario uses.

setup.why: godmode ON tops HP up every tick and masks every HP effect.

enemies.why: Level 8, HP 48, ATK 64 -- the hardest config enumerable from this repo. Two of them against one low-level character reliably wipes the party.

steps.label: the Vampiric acts once, then the demons are allowed to kill it

tells.expect: the party HUD card reads "Vampiric" -- our class, not a vanilla one
two demon bodies on the enemy side

steps.label: hand the fight to the enemies until the party is down
the defeat RESOLVES -- summary, no wedge, no exception

tells.expect: the defeat / adventure-summary panel naming the Vampiric character -- it must still be OUR class on the summary, not a vanilla name
a grave/cross portrait, which means genuinely downed. Note godmode restores HP WITHOUT clearing the downed flag, so a full HP bar under a grave icon is not a rendering bug
the summary screen names the Vampiric character
an actual rendered screen. A pure-black frame here is the post-combat modal blocker dimming the venue -- it wedged a soak for 45 minutes presenting as a crash. Do not file it as evidence of anything
